reviews.decision_reason: The selection step treats every corpus row as demand-bearing because each has demand_score >= 3, but the supplied package contains only asserted need text, source ids, weights, and scores. It does not expose observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes to support those demand claims, so the boundary admits unsupported market-demand evidence into the trusted path.

Normalization preserves all allowed record ids and applies the bounded eight-row window, but the visible semantic evidence is insufficient to judge whether the retained rows are valid market-demand evidence. It carries forward rows whose demand basis is unsupported rather than making the missing evidence visible.

Given the normalized input it receives, provenance assembly deterministically ranks records by descending demand_score and record_id tie-break, then emits evidence source handoff records. No local contradiction is visible in this boundary; the unsupported demand basis originates upstream.
